title.en: Completed past actions and the ने (ergative) rule

summary.en: In completed past tenses, intransitive verbs agree with the subject—while transitive verbs mark the doer with ने and agree with the object instead.

body.en:
From *आँगन हवेली*, season 1.

When an action is finished and complete, Hindi uses the **perfective participle** (`-आ / -ए / -ई / -ईं`, plus five classic irregulars worth knowing by heart: *किया* from *करना* 'to do', *दिया* from *देना* 'to give', *लिया* from *लेना* 'to take', *गया* from *जाना* 'to go', and *हुआ* from *होना* 'to become/happen').

How the verb agrees depends on one golden split:

1. **Intransitive verbs (and motion/speech exceptions) NEVER take *ने*—the verb agrees with the subject:**
   - *दरवाज़ा खुल गया!* (`darvāzā khul gayā!`, 'the door opened!' — agrees with m.sg *दरवाज़ा*).
   - *तुम दस मिनट जल्दी आ गईं* (`tum das minaṭ jaldī ā gaīn`, 'you arrived ten minutes early' — agrees respectfully with Kavya).
   - Memorise four everyday transitive-looking verbs that behave like motion/intransitive verbs and **never** take *ने*: *लाना* ('to bring' — *काव्या नमकीन मक्खन ले आई*), *बोलना* ('to speak'), *भूलना* ('to forget'), and *समझना* ('to understand' — *मैं समझ गया* 'I get it').

2. **Transitive verbs mark the doer with *ने* (`ne`), and the verb agrees with the direct object!**
   - *आपने घंटी बजाई!* (`āpne ghanṭī bajāī!`, 'you rang the bell!') — *बजाई* is feminine singular to match *घंटी* ('bell', f.), no matter whether a man or a woman rang it!
   - *क्या ये हरी पत्तियाँ आपने ख़ुद उगाई हैं?* ('did you grow these green leaves yourself?') — *उगाई हैं* agrees with feminine plural *पत्तियाँ*.
   - *मैंने कल फ़ोन पर कमरा सात बुक किया था* ('I booked room seven by phone yesterday') — *किया था* agrees with masculine singular *कमरा*.
